No judging panel.
A scoreboard.
Nothing here is a matter of opinion, and nobody can hide.
Not a Nintendo Switch.
$20,000
in total cash prizes
Compete for actual money and put your work in front of companies looking for people who can build.
Each track pays
$5,000
to the winner. Winner takes all. Second place gets nothing.
One side prize is our call, not the scoreboard's:
$100
for the best video about your weekend. Upload it to YouTube as Unlisted and enter it from
your team page
by
Nov 22
at
11 AM
ET.
A winning result can come from anyone. Bring yours.
Real people.
Real builds.
You can be virtual for the whole thing. Kickoff and the closing ceremony are in person if you want to come. Build from wherever you work best.
Anywhere
Build from anywhere
Work remotely or grab a table. The leaderboard and the team chat stay open the whole way through.
Nov 20
Not a minute before.
Kickoff at 6:00 PM ET in Evans Lab 1008
Every track opens online at the same moment, so you can start from anywhere.
Nov 22
Ceremony at 12 PM ET in Hitchcock Hall 131
The leaderboards freeze and the top team in each track gets paid.
Four problems.
Pick yours.
Every track is a problem a real company has today, and that company decides how it is measured.
They bring the problem. You bring the fix.

The rules.
Anything not answered here, email
hi@joinbuilders.org
.
Who can enter
Any current student, at any school in any country. Register with your school email.
Teams
Up to two people, or enter on your own. Each person is on one team.
Where you build
Anywhere. You can be virtual for the whole thing, from kickoff to the final. Kickoff and the closing ceremony are in person at Ohio State, but you don't have to attend either one to compete or to win.
When the problems come out
Every track opens online at
6:00 PM
Eastern
on
Nov 20
, the moment kickoff starts. Sign in on this page and open a track for its brief and starter files. No team sees a problem before then.
Tracks
Enter as many tracks as you like. One team can win more than one.
Tools
Use any tools you like, AI included, unless a track's page says otherwise.
Scoring
Every submission is scored automatically, and the live leaderboard shows each team's best practice score. Each track's page gives its metric, its tie rule and how many practice runs you get an hour.
The final
Submissions close at
11 AM
Eastern
on
Nov 22
. Your final entry for a track is the submission you pick, or your best-scoring one if you don't pick. See your track's page for how its final is scored. Organizers verify the top results before announcing them.
Prizes
The best final score in each track wins $5,000, and second place gets nothing. Teams anywhere in the world can win. Winners are paid online, in the room or not.
License
Anything built in this hackathon must be released under the MIT License. Builders may show your team's name, demo, screenshots and project description to promote the Buildathon.
Code you bring
You can use open-source libraries and code you wrote before the weekend. If your track takes a repository, name them in its README.

The Buildathon

The weekend
The tracks
The rules
Leaderboard
Pick a track
Explore
the four tracks
and open the ones you want to build for. You can enter as many as you like.
What’s on a track page?
Track pages open at kickoff,
Nov 20
at
6:00 PM
ET. Each has the problem and starter kit, plus the rules for scoring and the final.
Submit your work
Hand in your entry on the track page. Your team’s list shows your place in the queue as the scorer builds and scores it.
Submission limits
Each track accepts one entry per team at a time, including entries waiting in line. Every submission counts toward the track’s hourly limit, even a rejected one. The form shows how many you have left and when the next one frees up.
See your result
Open your submissions on the track page to read the score and feedback. If an entry is rejected, you’ll see why. Your best score stays.
Choose your final entry
Pick the submission you want in the final before the cutoff. If you leave it unpicked, your best-scoring entry goes through.
Read the leaderboard
Find your team on the
leaderboard
. Each track has its own board. Practice standings update every few seconds. Only the final decides the prize.
How to read the scores
Expand a board to see every team’s rank and best score. The board names the metric and tells you which direction is better. An earlier submission wins a tie.
The Baseline row is a simple reference entry’s score. Teams above it have beaten it. Once a track publishes its final results, its practice standings fold beneath them.
Ask for help
Sign in to ask a question in
leaderboard chat
, or email
hi@joinbuilders.org
if it is private. For a scoring delay, check your track’s queue on the
status page
.
Chat and announcements
You post under a handle that keeps your name and team private. Announcements appear on the same page. The status page also shows the scoring fleet.
Finish on Sunday
Submissions close
Nov 22
at
11 AM
ET
. Your final entry locks then.
Closing ceremony
Meet in
Hitchcock Hall 131
at
12 PM
ET
for the closing ceremony. Each track’s winner takes
$5,000
, and the best video entered on your team page takes
$100
.
Mech Royale
by
Builders
Hand in a GitHub repository with a Dockerfile at its top.
4 submissions an hour.
Final:
The top 32 teams on the practice board play a qualifying round, and the top 16 play a 64-match final series on new seeds (last 4 live). The series alone decides.
Shopping Sessions
by
Databricks
Hand in a GitHub repository with a Dockerfile at its top.
2 submissions an hour.
Final:
Your chosen commit is rebuilt and timed 3 times on about 60 million new events, and the fastest entries are retimed alone on one idle machine. Aim for under about 60 seconds in practice: if any final run goes over 3 minutes, you get no final score.
CAD De-ID
by
Machina
Hand in the S3 folder of one attempt.
2 submissions an hour, 20 scored attempts in all.
Final:
The board at the cutoff is final: your best attempt keeps its score, and nothing new is graded at the cutoff.
Blast Radius
by
RWX
Hand in a GitHub repository with a Dockerfile at its top.
1 submission an hour.
Final:
Your chosen commit is scored on unseen changes, and the top entries are rescored one at a time on one idle machine. Only the final counts.

94
of

unseen test cases passed
Nobody scores your pitch, because there is no pitch. The best result wins.
One problem. One number.
Each track is a real company problem with a published scoring rule. Find the cause of a failed build: accuracy on the same 100 test cases, higher wins.
Submit. Get scored.
Your code runs on test cases you have never seen. Nobody pitches and nobody grades a slide.
The board moves live.
Every submission updates the leaderboard. Build from anywhere and talk with the other teams in live chat while it happens.
You can see why they won.
First place is the highest score, and the score is on the board for everyone to read.
